name: Batch render and cache
summary: Render many cards with 2 parallel workers and a content-hashed frame cache, redraw only what changed, resume interrupted runs, and prove the frames are identical.
qualityBar: Batch framesHash equals the engine's renderCard framesHash for the same card
A repeat run does nothing (status unchanged, 0 frames drawn, under 3 s); a deleted mp4 is re-encoded from cached frames
A small edit with a changed-seconds hint redraws only those frames (tt10 closer edit: 105 of 495) and the result equals a full engine render; a wrong hint is rejected by an 8-frame check
After a simulated crash and a truncated frame the rerun resumes, repairs the bad frame and gives the same framesHash as an uninterrupted render
determinismReport passes for clean cards and the ported tt10 and fails, naming frames, for a card using Math.random
verifiedBy: 2026-11-19: node test.mjs exit 0 at full size (44 checks passed, 0 failed, about 2 min). Batch framesHash equals the engine's for the same card; repeat run 0.3 s; incremental edit redraws 21 of 60 frames (small card) and 105 of 495 (ported tt10, 11 s vs 24 s first render, preview) and equals a full engine render; wrong hint rejected; crash + truncated frame resumed with the same hash; determinismReport true for clean cards and ported tt10, false for Math.random. Demo rendered 1080x1920, 8.0 s, silent, checker passed (16 transient warnings from pop-in scaling). I viewed out/contact.png and judged it good. NOT checked: the equality of tt10's incremental result with a full engine render (only the 60-frame card is proven that way; tt10 is checked by the 8-frame sample plus the frame counts); full-size (1080x1920) batch runs of many cards (batch tests use 540x960 previews); mp4 byte identity with the engine's mp4 (frames are identical, encoder threads differ); never run with more than 2 workers; motion judged from stills, not played back.
